batchName: Roman Religion and Mythology (753 BC-AD 391) - Hard Batch 1

questions.question: For the augurs, what did the word *templum* originally mean?
options: The residence of the chief priest
A sacred space marked out by ritual
questions.explanation: The augurs worked inside a ritually marked sacred space, the templum. The word only later came to mean a temple building.
questions.sourceQuote: They worked within a sacred space marked out by ritual, called a *templum*, a word that only later came to mean a temple building.

questions.question: What did Augustus do for the Vestal Virgins? (select all that apply)
options: Gave them seats of honour at the games
Freed them from their vow of chastity
Placed them under the Senate's authority
Allowed them to marry after ten years
questions.explanation: Augustus raised the Vestals' funding and their public profile. The order survived well into the Christian era, until Theodosius put out Vesta's fire.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus, the first emperor, boosted their funding and gave them seats of honour at the games.

questions.question: Which of these events took place in AD 391?
options: Constantine's death as a deified emperor
Theodosius ending state support for other cults
questions.explanation: In 391 Theodosius ended state support for all other cults and put out the Vestals' fire. He had already made Christianity the official religion in 380.
questions.sourceQuote: In 391 he ended state support for all other cults and extinguished the Vestals' sacred fire.

questions.question: Christians kept attending the February ancestor festival of the Parentalia for centuries. In which year did a church council finally forbid it?
questions.explanation: The Parentalia lasted several days each February and honoured family ancestors. It was popular enough to outlive the official end of the old cults by well over a century.
questions.sourceQuote: It was so popular that Christians were still attending it centuries later, until a church council forbade it in AD 567.

questions.question: What did Romans require of the spoken prayer that accompanied every sacrifice?
options: It had to be sung in Greek
It had to be whispered so no one else heard
It could be skipped if the offering was large
Only the god's name needed to be spoken
Its words had to be exact, down to the god's proper title
questions.explanation: Correct form was everything in Roman religion. Public prayers were recited loudly by a priest on behalf of the whole community, and a single slip could spoil the ritual.
questions.sourceQuote: Every sacrifice needed a spoken prayer, and the words had to be exact, down to the god's proper title.

questions.question: The Capitoline temple had three chambers. Which deity occupied the right-hand one?
questions.explanation: Minerva was on the right, Juno on the left and Jupiter in the middle. Copies of the temple sprang up across Italy and the provinces.
questions.sourceQuote: The triad's great temple stood on the Capitoline Hill above the Forum, with three separate chambers: Juno on the left, Minerva on the right, Jupiter in the middle.

questions.question: Why could the flamen of Jupiter, a priesthood credited to Numa, barely pursue a political or military career?
options: He was forbidden ever to leave the temple
He was required to be a eunuch
He had to be born a Sabine
Strict rules of ritual purity bound him
He served for only one year
questions.explanation: Each flamen was devoted to a single god. Jupiter's flamen was hemmed in by such strict purity rules that a normal public career was almost impossible.
questions.sourceQuote: Jupiter's own flamen was bound by such strict rules of ritual purity that he could barely pursue a political or military career.

questions.question: Which measures did Augustus take as part of his religious revival? (select all that apply)
options: He ordered all subjects to sacrifice
He redirected vows for the Republic's safety to the emperor's wellbeing
questions.explanation: Augustus used religion to justify one-man rule. He restored priesthoods and took the title of chief priest, which later emperors kept, and vows once made for the Republic were now made for the emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: He restored old priesthoods, raised up the Vestals and became chief priest himself; later emperors kept the title.

questions.question: Which achievements did Roman tradition credit to Romulus? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Romulus was credited with the first temple to Jupiter and the first victory parade. The calendar, the Temple of Janus and the flamens were credited to Numa, and a later king built the temple to Diana.
questions.sourceQuote: Romulus was credited with Rome's first temple to Jupiter and its first victory parade.

questions.question: In 186 BC the Senate cracked down on a wildly popular cult and placed it under strict state control. Which god's rites were these?
questions.explanation: The Bacchanalia honoured the wine god Bacchus. Romans distrusted secret rites, even as mystery cults offering hope for the afterlife won growing followings.
questions.sourceQuote: In 186 BC the Senate cracked down on the Bacchanalia, the wildly popular rites of the wine god Bacchus, and placed them under strict state control.
